integration_recommendation: Integrate the eight frozen Lean modules as two explicitly scoped contracts after the required metadata corrections and root integration checks. They establish complete fp32 software-value execution and a natural-metadata allocator-parametric sequential logical host; they do not establish whole-original-program acceptance.

proven_scope.source: Exact existing TypedSource.original, with successful toAlgorithm? admission; no copied narrowed kernel and no replacement by TypedSource.blockFirst.
proven_scope.carrier: Word = FP.Value .fp32, a 32-bit value; the historical DSL .real tag is a cell/register channel, not the mathematical Real carrier.
proven_scope.value_parameters: Every natural M/N/K/BM/BN/BK and program ID in total logical memory, chosen FP.Config and valid ReductionPlan family.
proven_scope.host_parameters: Natural dimensions, blocks and tuning, plus an explicit non-numerical Allocator callback. Successful preparation derives positive blocks and source divisibility.
proven_scope.memory: Complete ordered per-program output scatter and pid0-fastest full 2D grid with previous actual/reference memory; whole-memory equality and frames.
proven_scope.acceptance_limit: Native allocation, caller Int/Python domain, byte addresses, compiler/launch admissibility and concurrency remain unproved.

semantic_findings.topic: Original source and full dynamic loop
semantic_findings.result: The Python source and Kernels.original agree on pids, row-major output tile, zero accumulator, K/BK loop bound, unmasked A and B offset formulas, broadcasting to BN×BM×BK, axis2 reduction, transpose, accumulator-first addition and final unmasked store. source is definitionally TypedSource.original. source_split identifies prologue, the original dynamic forRange body and tail. loop_correct inducts over every K/BK iteration, with no fixed K/BK, source-success or output premise. All loads precede the final store, so the invariant correctly retains program-entry memory throughout the reduction loop.
semantic_findings.limit: For BK=0 the total interpreter uses Nat division conventions and performs zero iterations; the wrapper rejects BK=0 after allocations. Arbitrary per-program dimensions/pids are not native launch/bounds claims.

semantic_findings.result: Word is FP.Value.fp32. engine supplies +0 literals, FP.mul, FP.add, identity payload fp32Load and explicit reduceSum. Structural evaluation dispatches the existing historical .real sum to reduceSum, and floating binary operations to the supplied add/mul; address operations stay Nat. treeValue evaluates each product/zero/add on concrete software words. memory_independent_of_unused_backend proves final memory cannot depend on any fallback Algebra callback.
semantic_findings.limit: fp32Load=id is payload preservation in this typed cell model, not a real-to-float identity law. Native rounding/FTZ/NaN behavior and compiler contractions are not certified by the software interpretation.

semantic_findings.result: ReductionPlan.valid in TermModel requires its tree leaves to be a permutation of every Fin n input exactly once plus its recorded zero padding. treeValue retains that exact tree, every zero seed and every FP.add. accumulated begins with fp32 positive zero and performs accumulator-first FP.add for successive blocks. No commutativity, associativity, additive-zero identity, real sum or reassociation premise is used.
semantic_findings.limit: The chosen family has one plan per length; actual compiled layout/tree/seed/fusion correspondence requires explicit numerical binding. The kernel proof does not assert all valid plans give the same bits.

semantic_findings.result: expectedMemory is a scalar fp32 product/tree/block recurrence followed by ordered output writes, independent of exec/source. bodyInvariant tracks the complete carry for arbitrary loop index and unchanged memory. tail_memory equates the actual final store with this reference, including aliases and repeated addresses in unrestricted parameter cases. The frame retains every cell outside the potential per-program write set.
semantic_findings.limit: This is a total tagged-cell memory reference. Wrong-tag reads follow Structural.Cell.read defaults; native physical storage interpretation is a separate obligation.

semantic_findings.topic: Complete actual grid with current memory
semantic_findings.result: The grid is exactly (M/BM,N/BN), traversed with pid0 fastest. runGridPrefix invokes the full actual source using fresh registers and previous program memory. referenceGridPrefix independently advances previous reference memory, so aliases across A/B/output observe preceding writes. Bounds/coverage establish the complete original coordinate set, and grid_correct proves successful full execution, exact final memory and a global outside-write-set frame.
semantic_findings.limit: Only the explicit sequential schedule is proved. Arbitrary native program order, instruction interleavings, races and physical alias behavior are not established.

semantic_findings.result: prepare requests randn[M,K], randn[M,N,K] and zeros[M,N], in that order, threading allocator-returned memory. It propagates each allocation failure before K/BK, then M/BM, then N/BN modulo/guard handling. Zero divisor errors occur at the source stage; successful Prepared records allocation results, regions, final memory, dimensions, positive blocks, divisibility and unchanged tuning. runWrapper launches from post-allocation memory, and its frame is correctly relative to launch.memory rather than pre-allocation memory.
semantic_findings.limit: Allocator is an unrestricted non-numerical primitive input. The request domain denotes fixed CUDA/fp32 by convention; no implementation proves fresh physical storage, zero initialization, random distribution, contiguous typed cells or error-side-effect correspondence. Except errors do not expose the heap/RNG state after earlier allocations, so no rollback or unchanged-memory-on-error result is claimed.

semantic_findings.result: tiled_coordinate_lt proves floor-grid tile coordinates stay below the declared extent, and row_major_bound composes them. all_unmasked_addresses_in_declared_extents proves A/B/output formulas under valid grid, loop and lane indices. complete_output_coverage and complete_inner_coverage cover every output coordinate and every K coordinate under the original positive/divisible host conditions.
semantic_findings.limit: The combined address theorem includes c:Fin(K/BK) and k:Fin BK even for its output conjunct. At K=0 that whole statement is vacuous, although output stores still occur. A non-vacuous output bound for this case follows from tiled_coordinate_lt plus row_major_bound, but this frozen batch does not expose it as a standalone output theorem. This review does not claim the combined theorem itself certifies zero-K output addresses. Native pointer widths/overflow/allocation bounds remain separate.

semantic_findings.result: The original batched_vecmat function has no dtype argument and all three allocations hard-code torch.float32. Therefore fp32 A/B/output is the complete enumerated wrapper dtype domain, not a selected subset of caller-provided tensor dtypes. The proof uses that same fp32 source and concrete fp32 carrier.
semantic_findings.limit: This dtype enumeration applies to the wrapper under the explicit allocator/storage representation boundary. It is not a theorem for arbitrary direct invocations of the generic Python kernel or arbitrary allocator-produced physical tensor representations.

nonblocking_precision_notes: Preserve the zero-K combined-bounds vacuity described above. A separately frozen no-K-premise output-bounds/uniqueness helper needs its own review and hashes; it is not part of this eight-source receipt.
Retain complete_enumerated_wrapper_dtype_domain only with its explicit fixed-fp32 wrapper interpretation and unbound allocator/storage boundary.
No data-distribution assumption is needed for functional correctness over every produced word. This does not validate RNG or allocator implementation.
Do not treat software total execution for zero/nonpower blocks as native specialization admission.
remaining_nondeferrable_gaps: Host Arguments use natural metadata; arbitrary Python types, negative dimensions/blocks/tuning remain outside the Lean host domain. Source probes confirm some negative blocks pass assertions and reach negative-grid or invalid-block dispatch.

Allocator is an explicit non-numerical callback for all three ordered fp32 CUDA requests. Native allocation failure behavior, fresh physical separation, contiguous fp32 cells and tensor-to-region/byte-memory/ABI representation remain unbound. Kernel correctness quantifies all produced words, requiring no RNG distribution law.
Address bounds and output/K coverage are proved for natural element indices. Fixed-width sizes, intermediate overflow, storage representation and native pointer correspondence remain open.
Native block/arange/resource legality, empty grids and zero-K specialization admission, and supported num_warps/num_stages remain open; Python accepts some non-power-of-two blocks and invalid tuning.
Complete grid is one explicit sequential pid0-fastest schedule. Native allocation freshness, race freedom and concurrent schedule refinement remain unproved.
Source equality uses the existing full admitted TypedSource.original transcription. Static source comparison and wrapper AST probes do not constitute a verified Python compiler translation.
numerical_bindings_eligible_for_explicit: Bind chosen FP.Config and concrete fp32 FP.add/FP.mul behavior to device rounding, FTZ, infinities/NaNs, signed zero and special-value handling.
Identify and bind actual native reduction tree and explicit padding/seeds to the supplied valid ReductionPlan at block_k.
Bind compiler fusion/reassociation and any operation contraction across product/reduction/block-accumulation boundaries; no equality to a real sum is assumed.

supporting_evidence.cpu_probe_scope: Exact original wrapper AST; CUDA requests recorded and serviced by real CPU allocations; Triton kernel replaced by launch recorder. No numerical output, GPU execution, native compiler, CUDA allocator or Lean cross-evaluation evidence.
